The elections will coincide with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[2022 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. {{toclimit|2}} == District 1 == {{Infobox election | election_name = 2022 Minnesota's 1st congressional district election | country = Minnesota | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | previous_election = 2022 Minnesota's 1st congressional district special election | previous_year = 2022 (special) | election_date = November 8, 2022 | next_election = 2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Minnesota#District 1 | next_year = 2024 | image_size = x150px | image1 =Brad Finstad 117th Congress (cropped).jpeg | nominee1 = [[Brad Finstad]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = 3x4.svg | nominee2 = [[Jeff Ettinger]] | party2 = Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | image3 = 3x4.svg | nominee3 = Richard Reisdorf | party3 = Legal Marijuana Now Party | popular_vote3 = | percentage3 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Brad Finstad]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{see also|Minnesota's 1st congressional district}} The 1st district stretches across southern Minnesota from its borders with [[South Dakota]] to [[Wisconsin]], and includes the cities of [[Rochester, Minnesota|Rochester]], [[Mankato, Minnesota|Mankato]], [[Winona, Minnesota|Winona]], [[Austin, Minnesota|Austin]], [[Owatonna, Minnesota|Owatonna]], [[Albert Lea, Minnesota|Albert Lea]], [[New Ulm, Minnesota|New Ulm]], and [[Worthington, Minnesota|Worthington]]. The incumbent was Republican [[Jim Hagedorn]], who was reelected with 48.6% of the vote in 2020.{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Cheryl L.|title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 2020|url=http://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/Election-Statistics/|publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives]] | date=February 28, 2019}} The seat is currently held by [[Brad Finstad]], who won the special election held on August 9th after Hagedorn died on February 17, 2022.{{Cite web|date=2022-02-18|title=Congressman Jim Hagedorn Dies: 'He Lived His Dream By Serving Others'|url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2022/02/18/congressman-jim-hagedorn-dies-he-lived-his-dream-by-serving-others/|access-date=2022-02-18|language=en-US}} === Republican primary === ==== Candidates ==== ==== Nominee ==== * [[Brad Finstad]], incumbent U.S. Representative, former Minnesota Director of [[USDA Rural Development]], and former state representative{{Cite web|last=Fischenich|first=Mark|date=March 7, 2022|title=Finstad, Munson join special congressional election|url=https://www.mankatofreepress.com/news/local_news/finstad-munson-join-special-congressional-election/article_f92b84ae-9e57-11ec-9ed7-c77466fce181.html|access-date=March 7, 2022|website=[[The Free Press (Mankato)|The Free Press]]}}{{Cite web|url=https://finstadforcongress.com/|title=Finstad for Congress|website=Finstad for Congress}} ==== Eliminated in primary ==== * [[Jeremy Munson]], [[Minnesota House of Representatives|state representative]]{{cite news |title=State rep.
